rewrites.//: Must come FIRST. Rewrites match in order, and the SPA catch-all below would otherwise swallow every API call and return index.html - which surfaces as "Unexpected token '<'" when the client parses HTML as JSON, and points nowhere near the actual cause.
SPA fallback: deep links like /estimates/abc-123 are client-side routes with no file behind them. Without this they 404 on refresh.

headers.//: Catch-all, deliberately first. Every header block that matches is applied and later blocks win, so the more specific rules below override this. A rule matching only /index.html is not enough: headers match the ORIGINAL request path, not the rewritten one, so real traffic to / and /estimates never matched it and fell back to Firebase's default max-age=3600. That left browsers holding a stale index.html for an hour after each deploy, pointing at hashed asset filenames that no longer exist - a white screen with no server-side symptom.
Hashed filenames, so they can be cached indefinitely. A new build produces new names.
Referenced by index.html as the favicon and by every Resend email template via Settings.logo_url. The filename is not content-hashed, so this cannot be immutable - a day is the compromise.
